title: Monolithic Error Enums
damaged_code:
```rust
enum AppError {
    DatabaseDisconnect,
    RowNotFound,
    InvalidJson(String),
    ValidationError(String),
    EmailSendFailed,
    FileSystemFull,
    S3Timeout,
    // A single enum holding errors for database, parsing, validation, and network!
}
```
pattern: A single, massive error enum containing every I/O, parsing, network, validation, and domain error variant in the entire application codebase.
why_bad: Directly violates encapsulation and compile-time boundaries. A minor validation check change forces a recompilation of the entire codebase and couples every module to a single massive error file. It also prevents local reasoning, as a simple validation helper signature implies it can return S3 network timeouts.
detection: Look for a single enum containing more than 20 distinct error variants representing disjoint subsystems (such as databases, third-party APIs, and parsing libraries).
counterexample: `Context-dependent`. Application-root error adapters inside binary crates that exist solely to map disparate module errors for final logging at the program boundary.
fix: Define small, localized error enums for each module or crate, mapping them at boundaries if needed.
source: *Robert C. Martin - Clean Architecture (2017)*, Chapter 10; *Steve McConnell - Code Complete (2004)*, Chapter 7.
